name: Form
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: Title or heading that names the task

2.name: Way out (Cancel word, back arrow or X)

3.name: Picker, tick box, toggle, dropdown, chips or date wheel

5.name: Filled commit button at the bottom

7.name: Commit action in the top bar

8.name: Sheet with a rounded top edge

v1.name: Top bar actions
v1.lead: Cancel and Save in the top bar
expect: A way out and the commit action both sit in the top bar
No filled button at the bottom of the page
A title that names the task
Text fields and pickers below the bar

v2.name: Labelled field page
expect: A way out and a title at the top
Text or number fields make up the page
One filled button to finish, not an action in the top bar

v3.name: Single choice
expect: A way out and a title at the top
One question answered with a picker, tick box, toggle or list
One filled button to confirm, usually at the bottom

v4.name: Amount or review
expect: A title that names the task
A text or number field and a picker for the choice
One filled button at the bottom to confirm

not_checked: What happens after the tap on the commit control: one screenshot cannot show it.
Whether an error line appears after a wrong entry, and whether the commit button wakes up once the needed fields are filled: that takes a second state.
Faint button labels are measured by the contrast rule on every screen; the switched-off look itself needs a reader, since a pale label alone does not mean the button is disabled.

rules.says: No submit control is in view: the keyboard covers it or the form scrolls past it.
rules.why: No submit control is in view because the keyboard covers it or the form scrolls. Seen on 5 of 60 checked screens.

rules.says: The commit button looks switched off and nothing says what is missing.
rules.why: The commit button looks switched off and nothing says what is missing. Seen on 10 of 60 checked screens.

rules.says: Tiny capital labels or a block of small print make the form hard to read.
rules.why: Tiny capital labels and day chips are hard to read (Done), and a block of small print comes before the question (Qantas Airways). Seen on 4 of 60 checked screens.

rules.why: 40 of 60 checked screens have "Picker, tick box, toggle, dropdown, chips or date wheel".

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern, or on the label of a greyed-out button (the guidelines leave out controls that cannot be used yet). Faint placeholder text in an empty field is only a hint, since iOS's own placeholder grey is about 1.7:1.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
